items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta Interview, 1957-03-21
items.q: He said, you ought to be playing clarinet. He said, you buy clarinet, I'm going to teach you for nothing.

ctx.x: Are you self-taught on that, or did somebody show you how to play saxophone?

Well, I'll tell you about saxophone. When I went over to Los Angeles, I asked Wayne Whaley, he was another fella. He said, you ought to be playing clarinet. He said, you buy clarinet, I'm going to teach you for nothing. So I bought a clarinet. So I bought a clarinet. And he, I bought a method book.

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: I take the job a week this place. Who they had out there but Mud Carey, Wade Whaley, and a little fella called Mack Hill

ctx.x: She won't bother anything. She won't bother anything. Let her play. I won't hurt anything.

Okay. All right. Go ahead now. So I says, all right, he's do favors for me. So I goes out to the bungalow at West End. And who they had out there, Walter Deku, well, I was playing this place a week. I take the job a week this place. Who they had out there but Mud Carey, Wade Whaley, and a little fella called Mack Hill stuck a bone on his feet. He died. The drum out there. Look at us out there. And I went there. So glad I came along because Wade used to buy music all the time and Walter Deku didn't read and he…

Well, I won it. And they throw it back to Sacramento, you see. Oh, yeah. And with a license of that kind, you can't, after 30 days, it's cancer. You can't use it, see. So it went back and it hit to the right because we couldn't get ready. You're all set to open the new place now. Yeah, he told me, go ahead. Well, I get it or not. We have the number, you know.
